name: Nueces Crossover Pipeline
researcher_notes: The EIA pipeline projects table for August 2026, sheet Historical Projects (1996-2024), Excel row 787, lists Nueces Crossover Pipeline. Operator is Energy Transfer Partners LP. It is an expansion in Texas, marked completed, in service December 2014. It states 51 miles, 800 million cubic feet per day capacity, and a cost of 114 million dollars. The sheet gives no diameter, no start or end point, and no FERC docket. A search snippet said 36-inch and Nueces to Live Oak County, but the Oil and Gas Journal article from 2012 does not name this pipeline, so the diameter and endpoints are not confirmed and are left blank. EIA is one source only, so no second independent source was found (web search was unavailable). It was checked against existing rows and is not NET Mexico (124 miles, Nueces County to Rio Grande City), Corpus Christi Pipeline (37 miles) or Valley Crossing. The length of 51 miles (about 82 km) clears the 25 km floor. No route was researched. Intrastate lines do not appear at FERC, so the Texas Railroad Commission should be checked for a second source and for endpoints. Owner uses the existing team entity Energy Transfer. The pipeline might be a piece of the Eagle Ford expansion already noted under P0224, which is worth a check.
